name: Mr. Backupsy
role: Looks after the backup — a bit nervous and anxious, so he checks everything three times
bubble.loading: One moment, I'm looking at the backup…
bubble.missing: I can't find the backup engine (unraid-backup), so there's nothing for me to do yet.
bubble.asleep: The engine's folder is on a sleeping disk — I don't dare wake it. Here's what I knew.
bubble.no_runs: There hasn't been a backup run yet. That makes me quite nervous.
bubble.running_kopia: I'm taking {share} offsite right now ({n} of {total}).
bubble.running_vm_shutdown: A backup is running — first I'm waiting for the VMs to shut down. The apps keep running meanwhile, nothing is stopped yet. I've asked nicely … and I'll ask again every minute!
bubble.running_check: I'm checking whether settings.ini still matches the server.
bubble.running_dryrun: I'm working out a dry run — nothing gets changed.
bubble.eta_rough: Done at about {time} — a rough guess: it's the first backup, there's nothing earlier to go by.
bubble.eta_late: It takes longer than usual — I expected it around {time}.
bubble.eta_partner_unknown: Done at about {time}, plus the step to the partner: it gets something for the first time, so I can't tell how long that takes yet.
bubble.first_eta: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time ({size}). That takes many hours, it isn't stuck, I've checked three times! It's read at ~{rate}/s — it should be through at about {time}.
bubble.first_soon: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time ({size}). Many hours — but now it's nearly through, any moment (read at ~{rate}/s). I'm watching!
bubble.first_measuring: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time ({size}). That takes many hours, it isn't stuck! I'm still timing how fast it's read …
bubble.first_nosize: Oh dear — {share} goes offsite for the very first time. That takes many hours, it isn't stuck — how many, I can't say: I don't know how big it is.
bubble.first_sent: And only {sent} actually sent so far?! … No, no, that's right, I looked it up: Kopia compresses, and what the repository already has it doesn't send twice.
bubble.last_ok: Phew! The last backup {when} went through without problems.
bubble.last_ok_kopia: Phew! The last backup {when} went through: {ok} of {total} saved offsite.

bubble.last_warnings.one: The last backup {when} ended with one warning.
bubble.last_warnings.other: The last backup {when} ended with {warnings} warnings.

bubble.last_errors.one: Oh no — the last backup {when} had one error. Please have a look at the log.
bubble.last_errors.other: Oh no — the last backup {when} had {errors} errors. Please have a look at the log.

bubble.last_failed: Oh no — the last backup {when} didn't finish.

bubble.old.one: That's more than a day ago.

bubble.no_schedule: Oh dear: no backup is scheduled! That makes me feel quite faint.

bubble.drift.one: One thing on the server changed since the setup.
bubble.drift.other: {n} things on the server changed since the setup.

aborting_wait.vm: Abort received ({when}) — I'm waiting until the VM is off (at most 5 minutes), then I start everything again and clean up.
aborting_wait.kopia: Abort received ({when}) — Kopia saves what it has, then I clean up.

check.setup_how: Mr. Backupsy → «Set up…»: he reads the server and proposes everything. (In a terminal: {path})
check.engine_trust: The backup folder and its settings belong to root alone
check.engine_trust_how: Not so for {path}: the backup engine refuses to run until it is — it works as root and reads nothing others could have written. In a terminal on the server: {cmd}
check.schedule_how: Mr. Backupsy → Schedule: pick a time.
check.kopia_how: For the offsite copy: install Kopia from ⟦Apps⟧ (e.g. imagegenius/kopia), connect it to your repository once in the KopiaUI, then read the server again in Mr. Backupsy's «Set up…».
check.kopia_running_how: Start it on the Docker page.
check.kopia_autostart_how: It isn't on autostart: after a reboot or an array stop Kopia stays off, and the next backup goes without its offsite copy. On the Docker page switch on «⟦Autostart⟧» for «{name}» — for a container of a Compose stack, the stack's autostart in Compose Manager's list below the containers.
check.kopia_root_how: Set PUID and PGID to 0 in the template of «{name}» (now {puid}) — otherwise everything only its owner may read is missing from the backup.
check.kopia_mapping_how: In the template add a path: ⟦Host Path⟧ {path}, ⟦Container Path⟧ e.g. /uso, ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧» (now: {now}). With plain «⟦Read Only⟧» Kopia sees empty folders. Kopia names its sources after the ⟦Container Path⟧ (/uso/<share>): changing it later makes new sources — in the same repository nothing is uploaded twice, but every file is read once more, and the old sources keep their history under the old names until you remove them in Kopia.
check.kopia_repo: Kopia is connected to its repository
check.kopia_repo_how: Connect the repository in the KopiaUI of «{name}», then click «Tour» at Mr. Backupsy.
check.kopia_emptied_how: The offsite copy is suddenly empty — snapshots on {when}: {before}, now: {now}, not deleted by the office. Possibly an attack or the wrong repository: since {since} nothing goes offsite (the local snapshots, packages and partners go on). If that wasn't you: delete nothing — Object Lock may still hold the data; the Consultant's Object Lock guide shows how to get it back through a second, read-only connection with --point-in-time. If the repository is really new, say so on Mr. Backupsy's page.
check.kopia_lock_extend: Kopia extends the Object Lock of «{name}»
check.kopia_lock_extend_how: The repository has Object Lock ({mode}), but Kopia's full maintenance or its extending of the locks is switched off — once its retention period is over, whatever never changes loses its lock, and the protection against ransomware is gone without a word. In the console of the container «{name}»: kopia maintenance set --extend-object-locks=true --enable-full=true
check.kopia_lock_lapse: Kopia's Object Lock doesn't run out
check.kopia_lock_lapse_how: Kopia last extended the locks on {last} — they run out on {until}, then the repository is no longer protected against ransomware. Kopia extends them only at its full maintenance, and only the maintenance owner runs it: now {owner}, this office's Kopia is {me}. Keep the Kopia server in «{name}» running; if the owner isn't {me}, in its console: kopia maintenance set --owner=me — then once right away: kopia maintenance run --full
check.kopia_lock_late: Kopia's full maintenance runs on time
check.kopia_lock_late_how: Kopia's full maintenance is late (it last extended the locks on {last}, they hold until {until}). Only it extends the Object Lock — if it stays away, the locks run out. Maintenance owner: {owner}, this office's Kopia: {me}. Keep the Kopia server in «{name}» running; if the owner isn't {me}, in its console: kopia maintenance set --owner=me
check.kopia_lock_never: Kopia has extended the Object Lock at least once
check.kopia_lock_never_how: Kopia has never extended the locks yet — its first full maintenance was due on {next} and hasn't run. Only it extends the Object Lock; without it the locks run out at the end of their retention period. Maintenance owner: {owner}, this office's Kopia: {me}. Keep the Kopia server in «{name}» running; if the owner isn't {me}, in its console: kopia maintenance set --owner=me

setup.bubble_have: These are your current settings, plus what I'd suggest for anything new. Change what you like, then apply.
setup.bubble_new: Nothing is set up yet. Here is what I suggest for this server — check it, change what you like, then apply.
setup.bubble_backup_runs: A backup is running — the setup waits until it is done.
setup.applying_long: Applying: checking, writing settings.ini, Kopia policies…
setup.applied_ok: Applied. settings.ini is written; the next run uses it.
setup.forget_text: I put your settings (settings.ini) and the decisions from this assistant aside, then propose everything as on a new server.
setup.forget_warn: Until you apply again, no backup runs — not on schedule either.
setup.forget_keeps: What is backed up stays: local snapshots, dumps and archives, what lies offsite (Kopia's snapshots and policies), the history. The old settings are then in state/reset-<time>/.
setup.forget_default: Your default for new things («{name}») goes too — the setup starts with my proposals again.
setup.forget_snapshots: Snapshots of shares you no longer back up afterwards stay where they are — you can clear them away at Ms. Snapshotini's.
setup.bubble_forgetting: I'm putting the old settings aside — then I start anew.
setup.forgotten: Forgotten — I'm looking at the server anew.
setup.forget_failed: Forgetting didn't work — see the messages below.
setup.apply_none: Nothing changed — applying writes the same settings again and lines up Kopia's policies.
setup.apply_new: Nothing is set up yet. This is how I set myself up:
setup.apply_hint: Mr. Backupsy checks everything again, keeps the previous settings.ini, writes the new one and — if backups go offsite — lines up Kopia's policies. The schedule stays as it is.
setup.apply_hint_new: Mr. Backupsy checks everything again, writes settings.ini and — if backups go offsite — Kopia's policies. No backup starts.
setup.apply_responsibility: After the first runs, check that everything you need is really in the backup, and try a restore now and then — a backup can be faulty or incomplete, and your data stays your responsibility.
setup.proposal_tip: A proposal of Mr. Backupsy's — you didn't change anything here.

setup.declined.one: 1 proposal you declined — I don't make it again while it stays the same:
setup.declined.other: {n} proposals you declined — I don't make them again while they stay the same:

setup.filter.only_new_hint: Show only the rows marked new or waiting for your decision
setup.filter.none: Nothing in this step fits the filter.

setup.key_unknown: the entry «{key}», which Mr. Backupsy doesn't know, goes
setup.key_unknown_tip: Written into settings.ini by hand. Apply writes the settings anew with what Mr. Backupsy knows — this line is not kept.
setup.key.general_mount_root: Where snapshots are mounted during a run
setup.key.general_view_root: Where btrfs snapshots can be browsed
setup.key.general_min_free_gb: Free space kept in the backup place (GB)
setup.kopia_sub: Where the backups go, the flash, and whether they also go offsite (encrypted with Kopia: S3, Backblaze B2, SFTP, WebDAV, a NAS …). Without an offsite copy everything stays on this server — that helps against deleting by mistake, not against fire, theft or a dead server.
setup.kopia_on_hint: Encrypted with Kopia: S3, Backblaze B2, SFTP, WebDAV, a NAS … You connect Kopia to that storage once in the KopiaUI — passwords and keys never go into these settings.
setup.kopia_recheck: Offsite was off so far, so I haven't checked Kopia yet. Apply, then read again — then I check the container, the mapping and the repository.
setup.k_probe_0: Kopia sees new snapshot mounts right away
setup.k_probe_1: Kopia does NOT see new snapshot mounts
setup.k_caretaker: The team lead explains what to do.
setup.k_hostid: Kopia's host name is a container ID — after re-creating «{name}» all sources would look new. Set a fixed host name in the KopiaUI.
setup.k_problem.no_container: There is no Kopia container for the offsite copy. Install one from ⟦Apps⟧ (e.g. imagegenius/kopia) and connect it to your storage in the KopiaUI.
setup.k_problem.container_gone: Kopia's container {name} is gone. Make it anew from its template (⟦Docker⟧ → ⟦Add Container⟧, template {name}) — until then nothing goes offsite.
setup.k_problem.docker_off: Docker is switched off — the offsite copy needs it, because Kopia runs in a container. You can switch Docker on under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Docker⟧.
setup.k_problem.not_running: «{name}» is not running — start it on the Docker page.
setup.k_problem.no_mapping: «{name}» has no mapping for {root}. Add the path {root} → {root} with ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧».
setup.k_problem.propagation: The mapping of {root} in «{name}» doesn't pass on what is mounted below it — Kopia would see empty folders. Set ⟦Access Mode⟧ «⟦Read Only - Slave⟧».
setup.k_problem.probe: «{name}» doesn't see new mounts under {root}. Re-create the container after changing the template.
setup.k_problem.no_repo: «{name}» isn't connected to a repository yet. Connect it once in the KopiaUI, then read again.
setup.k_problem.not_root: «{name}» doesn't run as root — set PUID and PGID to 0 in its template, otherwise files only their owners may read are missing.
setup.shares_sub: What steps 1 and 2 decide is greyed out. You decide the rest here. Big shares are proposed as "not backed up"; a new setup sends nothing offsite on its own — you pick what goes there.
setup.why.system: Docker image and libvirt.img — Unraid pulls the containers again, the run saves the VM configuration separately; no snapshot needed
setup.why.domains: VM disks — inconsistent while VMs run; back VMs up separately
setup.why.domains_snap: VM disks — local snapshot; how each VM is held for it, you set below under VMs
setup.why.timemachine: Time Machine target ({arg}) — holds other computers' backups
setup.why.timemachine_name: probably a Time Machine target (going by the name) — would hold other computers' backups
setup.why.kopia_workdir: Kopia's own config, cache or repository
setup.why.big_container: container data, big ({size}) — leave out the big folders in the details
setup.why.size_unknown: size unknown — measure or decide on purpose
setup.why.no_snapshots: no snapshot possible here (e.g. XFS) — Kopia (offsite) reads it live, or leave it out
setup.why.gone: doesn't exist any more — entry will be removed
setup.f_retention_hint: Empty = like all shares. Example: «7 0 0» keeps a week; the long history then comes from the offsite copy.
setup.f_kopia_retention: Kopia keeps (latest hourly daily weekly monthly annual)
setup.f_kopia_retention_hint: Six numbers or «inherit»; empty = like all shares.
setup.f_ignore: Kopia leaves out (one rule per line, relative to the share)
setup.f_folders: Folders in this share (with the containers that use them) — click to have Kopia leave one out or take it back:
setup.f_folders_none: No folders to click here — rules go into the field “Kopia leaves out”.
setup.f_folders_many: Too many folders to list them all — write rules into the field “Kopia leaves out”.
setup.f_folders_asleep: Not looked at on {disks}: asleep, I did not wake it — folders only there are missing here.
setup.f_folder_on: left out — click to back it up again
setup.f_folder_off: backed up — click to leave it out
setup.f_method_hint: auto = from a snapshot; live = read the running share (only if snapshots aren't possible).
setup.f_children_hint: Unticked datasets are neither snapshotted nor backed up.
setup.containers_sub: For the seconds of the snapshots, containers that write into backed-up shares are stopped — then the snapshot is clean, not just crash-consistent.
setup.ct_kopia: always keeps running · never backed up itself
setup.app_kopia_text: Kopia's own folders (configuration, cache, logs) are not needed for a restore. All it needs is its template — backed up with the flash, or new from Community Apps if need be (the consultant shows how under "Install by hand" — also after a total loss) — and your access data: repository password, storage (bucket, endpoint, access key and secret) and the KopiaUI login. Keep them apart from the server, e.g. in a password manager and on paper — without them you cannot reach your backups in an emergency.
setup.ct_risk_hint: This container writes into backed-up data; if it keeps running, its snapshot is like pulling the plug. Apps with their own SQLite database (Emby, Jellyfin, Plex, *arr …) are only clean when stopped.
setup.ct_volumes_hint: Docker volumes live in Docker's own folder and are NOT in the backup. Map a path into a backed-up share instead.
setup.ct_volumes_cache_hint: These Docker volumes only hold a cache (downloaded models, thumbnails, temporary files). They are not in the backup — that is fine: after a restore the app fetches their contents again by itself.
setup.ctwhy.media_server: media server — keeps running so streams aren't cut off (writes to {arg})
setup.databases_sub: MariaDB/MySQL, Postgres and MongoDB get a dump — taken after the apps have stopped, so dump and files match (Immich too, which has no maintenance mode). Readable, restorable into any version, checked right away. Nextcloud also goes into maintenance mode.

help.run: A backup run, step by step
help.run_text: Every run goes through these steps in order. First I look around. Then come the database dumps. VMs that shut down go first, while the apps still run. Then the apps stop, so dumps and files match. Then come the snapshots; containers are stopped for a few minutes. Then the copy goes offsite with Kopia. Last, I tidy up. The bracket under the steps shows when apps and VMs are held. «Done at about» and «last» come from how long earlier runs took. A source going offsite for the first time is different: I reckon it from its size and how fast it is read now.
help.results_text: How a run ended. «not finished»: it stopped unexpectedly, for example through a restart or because it was killed. «stopped»: you stopped it. «stopped» with «array stop»: it ended on purpose because the array was being stopped. Nothing is lost, and the next run continues. «skipped»: it didn't start, because another run, the setup or a restore still had the engine. A skipped run changed nothing, and the next run backs up as usual. The log has the details.
help.protection_text: Every share and how the backup protects it. The labels are the same everywhere in the office:
help.buttons_text: The tour compares the server with the settings. It takes seconds and changes nothing. Back up now offers three choices: a full run, one without the offsite upload, or a dry run. A run keeps going when you close the page. Stop ends it cleanly: containers come back, mounts go.
help.setup: I read the server and show proposals with reasons. You change what you like and apply. It all happens in the browser.
help.history: The last runs with their result. You see how much went offsite and how long containers were stopped. A click on a run opens its log.
help.drift: New shares or containers since the setup, or settings that don't fit any more. «Set up…» takes them over.
help.restore: Where the local snapshots, the offsite copy (Kopia) and the packages are. Bringing things back is Mr. Restori's job. He does it per app and VM, with ready-made commands.
disclaimer: No backup is a guarantee: a backup can be faulty or incomplete. You stay responsible for your data and your backup strategy — test a restore now and then and keep more than one copy (for example 3-2-1: three copies, on two kinds of storage, one of them offsite).
help.draft_text: Everything here is a draft until you press Apply at the bottom. Discard goes back to what was read. If there are only my proposals, Discard sets them aside until I read the server again.
help.replan: I read the server again: shares, containers, databases and Kopia. Nothing changes.
help.reasons_text: Every proposal says why: as before, new, too big, Time Machine target, Kopia's own folder …
help.details: Per share: the local and the Kopia retention, the method and the child datasets. Also the folders Kopia leaves out; the share's folders are one click away.
help.apply: First you see every change. Then I check again, keep the previous settings.ini, write the new one and line up Kopia.
help.forget: Puts your settings and the default aside and starts the assistant as on a new server. Nothing backed up is deleted. No backup runs until you apply again. The button is at the top right.
schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.intro: I enter the schedule with Unraid; Unraid then starts the run itself — even when nobody has the office open (only while the array runs). Best pick a time nobody needs the server: containers pause briefly for the snapshots.
schedule.custom_hint: Five fields as in User Scripts "Custom", e.g. 0 3 * * 1-6 (Monday to Saturday at 3 am).
schedule.examples_tip:
15 * * * * — every hour at quarter past
0 * * * * — every hour on the hour
0 */6 * * * — every 6 hours (0, 6, 12 and 18 o'clock)
0 1,12 * * * — every day at 1 am and at noon
0 3 * * 1-6 — Monday to Saturday at 3 am

help.rules_text: A click on a share shows its rules. You see what Kopia leaves out and how long it keeps versions. You see the share's own rules and the ones every share inherits. You see what stays on this server. And you see whether Kopia is really set up like that, as of the last tour. Change these rules only here, with «Change…» or «Set up…». Don't change them in the KopiaUI. I write these rules into Kopia myself. Whatever is changed there by hand, I report as drift, and the next Apply sets it back. Kopia thins out old versions itself, following these rules.

policy.skipped: Kopia lacks one of this share's own rules, so the run leaves the share out (it would upload more than wanted) — Apply in «Set up…» fixes it.

help.vms_text: A VM's disks are in the snapshot of its share, usually domains. What matters is how a running VM is treated for the seconds of the snapshot. There are four ways. «freeze» is best: the guest agent flushes and freezes the file systems. «pause» stops the VM for those seconds. «shut down» stops it cleanly; that takes minutes. «keep running» doesn't stop it; the copy is then only crash-consistent. A VM in a dataset of its own can also be left out. It can also keep its snapshots longer or shorter. You set this in «Set up…» → VMs. With a partner office the switch has five fields. «local + partner» sends the VM's own ZFS dataset to the partner after every run. «local + partner + offsite» does both. These fields are grey where the VM shares its dataset.
setup.vms_sub: Which VM do you need back when a disk dies? VMs that are backed up are paused or frozen for the seconds of the snapshot; their share gets a snapshot for it.
setup.vm_off_shared: Still inside the snapshot of "{share}", but without being held — and without restore help.
setup.apps_sub: A compose stack is one app. Apps that are backed up stop together for a moment for the snapshot, their databases are dumped first. Further shares of an app you tick yourself — they can grow fast.
setup.apps_docker_off: Docker is switched off — no apps to back up.
setup.apps_gone: Gone — in the settings, no longer on the server
setup.app_gone_had: It went offsite as a source of its own: {list}
setup.app_dump_hint: Before the snapshot the database is dumped and checked right away — part of the app when it is backed up.
setup.app_nodata_hint: This app binds no folder in a share. What is backed up is its template or compose file — it lives on the flash and goes with the flash backup.
setup.app_nodata_noflash: This app binds no folder in a share — only its template or compose file on the flash would be backed up. But the flash is not backed up.
setup.app_hold_hint: What the app does during the snapshot. Stop: it stops for a few seconds, its files are closed cleanly — the safest. Keep running: the snapshot catches its files in the middle of work, as if the power were cut. Databases usually cope with that; at worst the last seconds are missing. Good for media servers (running streams don't break off) and apps whose data hardly changes.
setup.app_dep_hint: the whole share is backed up, like the app
setup.app_dep_same: {share} is already backed up like the app — nothing to change.
setup.app_dep_kept: {share} stays at «{mode}» in step 3 — change it there.
setup.app_dep_step3_hint: You chose this share in step 3 already. Ticking it ties it to the app: it then follows the app's choice.
setup.level_hint.0: Not backed up: keeps running, no dump, nothing goes offsite. Its folder is still inside the snapshot of appdata.
setup.level_hint.1: Local snapshot; databases dumped first; template or compose file are backed up with the flash.
setup.level_hint.2: Like local, and offsite too — as a Kopia source of its own, with its own retention (step 4).
setup.level_hint.partner: Like local, and its ZFS snapshot to the partner office ({partners}) after every backup — only the blocks changed since the last one, encrypted on the way; the partner keeps it with its own retention.
setup.level_hint.partner_kopia: Like local, to the partner office ({partners}) and offsite as a Kopia source of its own — both.
setup.lock_hint: The VMs and apps above decide this. Change it there.
setup.lock_pkg: offsite — templates, dumps and VM configuration belong with what goes there
setup.ds_kopia: goes offsite too, because something is backed up there
setup.retention_sub: Two rows of numbers: how long local snapshots stay and how long Kopia keeps the offsite states. Dumps and configurations live inside those snapshots.
setup.r_kopia_hint: Latest, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, annual states. "inherit" = like Kopia's global policy.
setup.r_exceptions: Exceptions: per share in its details (step 3), per VM with a dataset of its own in step 1, offsite per app and VM right above.
setup.vm_service_off: The VM service is off — nothing to set up.
setup.vm_agent_hint.yes: qemu-guest-agent runs inside the VM: it can flush and freeze the VM's file systems for the snapshot.
setup.vm_agent_hint.no: The VM runs, but no guest agent answers. Freezing needs qemu-guest-agent inside the VM (for Windows: the virtio-win guest tools); until then pause is the safe choice.
setup.vm_agent_hint.channel: The VM is off, but a guest agent channel is configured — freezing should work when it runs.
setup.vm_agent_hint.none: No guest agent channel is configured for this VM.
setup.vm_tpm_hint: The VM has a virtual TPM. Its state is in the VM configuration archive next to the dumps.
setup.vm_gpu_hint: Passed-through hardware (e.g. a GPU). On another server its addresses differ — the VM's XML has to be adjusted there.
setup.vm_cannot_hint: No snapshot holds this disk, so the backup doesn't contain it.
setup.vm_shared_hint: Its disks lie in a dataset together with the share or other VMs: it always goes with the share's snapshot and can't be left out or kept apart on its own.
setup.vm_upload_hint: A VM's first upload offsite reads its disk files whole — the empty part of a sparse disk as zeros — so it reads {size}, though the files hold {used}. Once: later runs skip a file that didn't change. Local snapshots don't mind.
setup.vm_share_off_hint: The share holding its disks is set to off — so the VM isn't backed up either.
setup.vm_prep_hint: Freeze: the guest agent writes everything out and freezes the file systems for a moment (seconds). Pause: the VM stands still for the seconds of the snapshot. Shut down: cleanly before, started again after (minutes; never switched off hard).
setup.vm_ret_hint: How long this VM's snapshots stay: daily weekly monthly, e.g. 3 1 0 = three days, one week, no month. Empty = like the share “{share}” (the numbers in the field).
setup.vm_noagent_hint: Freezing needs the guest agent inside the VM. Without it the run pauses the VM instead.
vm.prep_text.freeze: Its guest agent flushes and freezes the file systems for the seconds of the snapshot; the VM keeps running.
vm.prep_text.pause: The VM stops for the seconds of the snapshot and then runs on — like pulling the plug, but no write is cut in half.
vm.prep_text.shutdown: Shut down cleanly before anything else stops and started again after the snapshot (minutes) — the apps don't wait for it. If it doesn't shut down in 5 minutes, it is paused for the snapshot instead — never forced off.
vm.prep_text.none: It keeps running: its disks in the snapshot are only crash-consistent, as after a power cut.
vm.not_set_up_hint: Its disks are in the share's snapshot, but nobody told Mr. Backupsy how to treat it — it keeps running (crash-consistent). «Set up…» → VMs.

help.packages_text: Every run writes one package per app and per VM to the backup place. An app's package holds its templates or compose files and its database dumps. A VM's package holds its XML, its UEFI variables and its TPM state. These are small files, and every run overwrites them. The data itself stays in the snapshots. The packages' history lies in the snapshots of the backup place's share. «Stale» is a package an earlier run wrote. Its app or VM is gone or no longer backed up. It is never deleted.

setup.place_none: Oh dear — there's no share here yet where I could keep my packages, and without one I back up nothing at all! I never make one myself: you decide where it lies. Please create one in Unraid — what matters is right below. I'll wait here.
setup.place_choose: Please choose a share for my packages above — or create a new one in Unraid. What matters is right below; I've checked it three times.
setup.place_title: What matters for the backup place
setup.place_1: Not on the pool appdata lies on — a failing pool would take the apps and their dumps together.
setup.place_2: Best a share on a ZFS pool, exclusive (Unraid gives it a dataset of its own there): only then do my packages' earlier backups live in snapshots, and only then may the place travel to a partner office too. A btrfs pool does for snapshots here, but never for a partner.
setup.place_3: Redundant if possible: a mirror pool. The array only as a last resort — there the share spreads over several disks, there's no snapshot of the whole and no partner, and on XFS only the last state stays.
setup.place_4: One place only: no secondary storage, no mover — the packages shouldn't wander between drives.
setup.place_5: It stays small: only configurations, database dumps, the flash archive and the VM configurations (often well under a gigabyte) — the big data stays in its own shares and their snapshots. No big disk needed; if it grows a lot, something is off (a huge dump, say). It needs no compression: my dumps are packed already.

help.waiting_text: What came after the last setup is backed up only locally, and it keeps running. A new container isn't stopped. A new VM isn't held. Then there are the shares for apps and VMs: appdata and domains, as Unraid names them in its Docker and VM settings. A new folder there that belongs to no app or VM, or to a new one, stays in the local snapshots. It doesn't go offsite. A new folder of an app or VM you already set up gets that one's level. A new folder in any other share simply follows its share. It goes offsite when the share goes offsite. You get one notification when a folder starts waiting. «Decide…» opens the setup. There you choose local or local + offsite, and Apply takes it over.

Until you apply, it is backed up only locally and keeps running; I never send it offsite or stop it unasked. With a default, I propose it at the default's level. Apply lists it separately under «New». A new folder in any other share goes with its share.
help.filter_text: The filter only hides rows; accents in names don't matter. It changes no decision and folds nothing you unfolded. It is empty each time you come. «Decide…» on my main page sets it to «Only what's new» and takes you to the first new thing.

help.preset_text: The default fills in the draft: my own proposals («Automatic»), «Everything local only» or «Everything local + offsite». If you already have settings, «Only to what is new» keeps them as they are. «Apply to everything now» gives every share, app and VM the default's level; on a new server it always applies to everything. Then I also switch on your boot device's backup (flash, Unraid's configuration) and your VMs' configuration, if they were off. Apply stores the default, and from then on whatever turns up later gets its level.
help.never: What I never back up on my own
help.never_text: A default changes nothing here either. The system share, Kopia's own folder, Time Machine targets and VMs that can't be snapshotted stay as they are. Under «local + offsite» a new share over 500 GB, or of unknown size, still waits for you. Media servers keep running during the snapshot. Your Kopia ignore rules stay.
help.partners_text: Then there is a fourth default: «Everything local + partner». It also sends every share and VM that is a ZFS dataset of its own to the partner, after every run. On the card «Everything local + offsite» the tick «also to …» does the same, next to the offsite copy.

help.tiles_text: The tiles are the page’s table of contents. Each tile sums up one section. A click shows that section alone. A second click, «◂ All» or «Show all» shows the whole page again. «Last backup» shows the backups. «Schedule» shows their time, with «Change…». «Protection» shows the whole table «Is everything protected?». The tiles for offsite, databases, packages, VMs and the flash (your boot device) show that table with only their rows. The line above the table names the filter. «Partners», «Changed» and «Restore» show their own sections. The section you open stays open at your next visit. A filter and the words in the bars are never kept. While a backup runs, its card stands in the tiles’ place and the whole page shows.

Close it for good — Unraid then leaves it alone: chown {uid}:users '{path}' && chmod 0770 '{path}'
